taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station T-14 (survey area T). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 161.1 | 3.39 | 3.39
2 | 1022.2 | 1.76 | 5.15
3 | 85.2 | 1.93 | 7.08
4 | 88.8 | 9.77 | 16.85
5 | 117.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as Q-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Station: T-14
Curve type: KH-type (file classification as Q-type is incorrect — resistivities rise then fall then rise again: 161.1→1022.2→85.2→88.8→117.4 Ω·m, not the monotonically decreasing sequence required for a true Q-type curve)
Aquifer depth: 5.15 m – 16.85 m (Layers 3–4, the low-resistivity zone between the resistive Layer 2 cap and the higher-resistivity Layer 5)
Recommendation: Target the screen/casing interval across 5.15–16.85 m, which corresponds to the conductive saturated zone; drill through the resistive 1022.2 Ω·m layer (3.39–5.15 m) with care, as it may represent a cemented/gravel horizon requiring harder-formation bit selection, and flag the file record for re-classification from Q-type to KH-type before finalizing the completion design.
